name: Coffee Brain
description: Coffee beside a brain is the status people send when thinking is still booting. It warns a meeting, answers a too-early text, or admits an idea only showed up after caffeine.
meaning: The cup is the fuel and the brain is the job that will not start without it. Together they mean "not ready to decide yet," unless the sentence is praising a point that woke the sender up.
examples: this plan only exists because of ☕🧠
seoDescription: What does ☕🧠 mean? It means the sender needs coffee before they can think, or that the idea arrived with the caffeine.

longForm.overview:
Coffee next to a brain is a status report. People send ☕🧠 when the mug is the only reason a thought is going to happen: before stand-up, on a red-eye, or in reply to a question that landed before the kettle boiled. The cup says fuel is still going in. The brain says output has not started, or has only just started, because of that cup. A lone coffee emoji can mean the drink tastes good. A lone brain can mean the idea is sharp. Stuck together, they mean the idea is not available yet, or that it should be trusted only as far as the caffeine has traveled.

The joke version points the other way. Drop ☕🧠 under a typo or a plan you wish you had waited to send, and it confesses the coffee failed. In a team channel that reads as a request for ten quiet minutes. On a friend's dawn text it complains about the hour. Written as "this take is ☕🧠," it praises a point that woke someone up. The words in front of the pair pick the reading. With no words, most people assume the weekday morning status, because that is the version that shows up in work chats every day.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
☕🧠 closes a check-in ("online, but ☕🧠"), sits under a photo of a mug beside an unopened laptop, or answers "you up?" with "barely." Remote teams use it to push a decision by one agenda item. Friends use it when a message did not need to be sent at sunrise.

It also rides with plans that depend on caffeine: a paper due at noon, a drive after a late shift, a design review that got booked at 8. The sender is not offering you a latte. They are telling you the quality of the next reply is sponsored by whatever is in the cup.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip ☕🧠 on news about someone's actual memory, focus, or diagnosis. The brain here is a joke about mornings, and it turns cruel next to real medical news. Skip it in a client email too. "My brain is not on" reads as careless once money is attached.

Also skip it when you only mean the coffee was excellent. A café recommendation wants the cup, or a savoring face, not a brain. And if you are complimenting a sharp idea that had nothing to do with caffeine, send the brain or a light bulb and leave the mug out.
longForm.howToReply:
If a teammate sends ☕🧠 before a meeting, start with status updates and hold the hard decision. Matching the pair back is friendly. Telling them to "just think" is the request they were postponing.

If it landed on your idea as praise, a short thanks is enough. If it landed on a message you sent at dawn, move the question to later. The pair is a delay request. It is not an insult about their intelligence, and answering it as one makes the morning worse.

faqs.question: What does ☕🧠 mean?
faqs.answer: ☕🧠 means thinking is running on coffee. Either the sender is not awake enough to decide, or the idea they are about to share showed up only after caffeine.

faqs.question: Is ☕🧠 an insult?
faqs.answer: Usually it is a status, not an insult. It becomes a jab only when someone sticks it on another person's bad idea, and even then the jab is about that idea.

faqs.question: What does ☕🧠 mean at work?
faqs.answer: In a work chat it asks for patience. The person is online, and they are telling you the first cup has not finished booting them.

faqs.question: What should I send instead of ☕🧠 for a good idea?
faqs.answer: Send 🧠 or 💡 when the coffee is not part of the story. Save ☕🧠 for the moment when the mug is why the thought exists.

conversationExamples.message: stand-up in 10, fair warning I am ☕🧠
conversationExamples.interpretation: They will join, but the first decision should wait. Open with status, not the hard call.
A complaint about the hour, not about you. Reply later or acknowledge that it was early.
A parent is home and not ready for questions. Give them the mug before the next ask.

conversationExamples.message: Saturday plan: walk first, decisions after ☕🧠
conversationExamples.interpretation: They want the date, and they want the restaurant picked once coffee has happened. Suggest a café stop.
A study post. "Good luck" fits. A new question does not.
